description: The bottom edge's integer program is L-natural-concave (separable concave plus concave functions of pairwise differences, over a box-and-difference domain), so a point that no +-chi_S move improves is the global integer maximum (Murota 2003, Thm 7.14), and the best move is an s-t minimum cut.  This replaces the concave relaxation's 1.563x bound with the exact integer maximum for every certified (pe, N).
open_gaps: tail lemma: blocks longer than N = 16 rows never exceed the N-row maximum
all-pe lemma: frames pe > 4 add nothing over pe <= 4

checks.name: M1 the split form is the committed G
checks.detail: 60 random integer points, pe 0..8, n 2..9: max |G - G_split| = 2.068e-25

checks.name: M2 zero-padding leaves G unchanged
checks.detail: max |G(u, 0^k) - G(u)| = 3.877e-25 for k = 1, 3, 7 — so an N-row program covers every block of length T <= N

checks.name: M3 every piece is concave at the integers
checks.detail: min second difference 2f(x) - f(x-1) - f(x+1) over the sampled pieces = 0.00012749

checks.name: M4 the min-cut move is the best move
checks.detail: 50 (point, sign) cases, n <= 9, all 2^n subsets: max |cut - brute force| = 2.585e-25, and the returned S attains it

checks.name: M5 every frame reaches a point no +-chi_S move improves
checks.detail: pe = 0..4 at N = 16 rows: max over frames 2.159802376118285961604.  The best NON-EMPTY move at any optimum gains -0.000759437, so the certificate does not rest on rounding (the gains are evaluated at mp.dps = 25).  The deepest support is 11 rows, well inside N.  By Murota's L-natural optimality theorem each is the exact integer maximum for its (pe, N); the BMAX = 10 enumeration recorded 2.159802376118285961604

checks.name: M6 the G1-free cut is enumerable for pe <= PEMAX, T <= N
checks.detail: cut 25 against the limit 32 (the relaxation bound gives 48).  CONDITIONAL on the tail lemma (T > 16) and the all-pe lemma (pe > 4); both open
